history.dynasty: Unknown founder; present structure much later
history.period: Believed ~400 years old (unrecorded date); 9th-century stone carvings in the complex
history.summary: The Bhairabi Temple stands at Kolibari on the outskirts of Tezpur, Sonitpur district, on a hillock overlooking the Brahmaputra and the Kolia Bhomora Setu. Goddess Bhairavi, one of the Mahavidyas of Durga, is worshipped here; locals call the shrine Maithan or Bhairabi Devalaya and regard it as an important Shakti Peetha / siddha pitha of Assam. Legend holds that Usha, daughter of the asura king Banasura, worshipped the Goddess at this spot. No record fixes the foundation date; local belief puts the temple at about 400 years old, while stone carvings on the premises are ascribed to 9th-century artistry (Bamuni Hills, about 2 km away, hold palace ruins of that era). The temple belonged to the Borthakur family of Tezpur and is now managed by the government through the District Deputy Commissioner's office. Traditional sacrificial offerings (goats, ducks, pigeons) continue. An earthquake reportedly tilted the structure and damaged a nearby building, briefly halting rituals — now resumed. name: Bhairabi Temple
town_description: Tezpur, headquarters of Sonitpur district on the north bank of the Brahmaputra about 175 km northeast of Guwahati, is one of Assam's oldest cities and a centre of mythology, archaeology and culture — 'the cultural capital of Assam'.

travel.railway: Tezpur railway station, about 6 km away
travel.road: At Kolibari on the outskirts of Tezpur, reached by a long staircase from the approach road; off NH 15

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Durga Puja/Navratri for the grandest celebrations
